newsitem.title: HONG KONG: WEEK AHEAD - HK stocks set to rebound after FOMC.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - HK stocks set to rebound after FOMC.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks may get the tonic they need to halt their downtrend this coming week with Tuesday's U.S. Federal Reserve meeting set to clear recent interest rate uncertainty, whatever the outcome, analysts said.
"Once the meeting is out of the way, despite what happens, I think people will buy on the news rather than sell on the news," said Andrew Fernow, director of research at Vickers Ballas.
"I think people have factored in the rate rise and you will see stocks rebounding off the levels you see now," he said.

Thirty-four of 48 Wall Street economists polled by Reuters last week said they expected the U.S. Federal Reserve to raise the key federal funds rate to at least 5.5 percent at the March 25 meeting from a current 5.25 percent.
In the run up to the meeting, Hong Kong stocks have taken a beating, with the Hang Seng Index retreating 247.23 points, or 1.94 percent, last week to close at 12,489.30 on Friday.
Since the start of this month, the blue chip Hang Seng Index has lost 909.42 points, or 6.79 percent, and is currently languishing at its lowest levels since late October 1996.
"If they announce a 25 basis point rise, Hong Kong will probably recover to around the 13,000 level, because I think it is just overdone," said ING Barings sales director James Osborn.
Analysts said corporate results released last week showed strong earnings growth and with interest rate uncertainty removed, investors would be able to focus on local fundamentals.
Henderson Land Development Co Ltd beat market expectations last week with a 33 percent rise in its interim net profit to HK$5.32 billion (US$687 million).
Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd posted interim net profit growth of 21 percent to HK$6.25 billion, and said it expects "considerable growth" for the full year.
"The results have been so good and the valuations as a result are looking better, and somebody is going to take notice. I think this selloff will end," said Fernow.
But he said trading may be cautious in the first days of the week ahead of the Fed meeting.

"Next week will be volatile," said Ben Kwong, director of research at Dharmala Securities. But he said the upside potential was greater than the downside, with share prices looking attractive at current levels.
"There is very good value in the market below the 12,500 level," Fernow said.
Major blue chip companies are due to continue reporting results during the week ahead.
COSCO Pacific Ltd is due to release its 1996 results on Monday and analysts expect strong net profit growth.
A slew of results are due on Wednesday including Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd, Hutchison Whampoa Ltd, CITIC Pacific Ltd, Shun Tak Holdings Ltd and Sino Land Co Ltd.

GITIC Enterprises Ltd is also set to make its trading debut on Wednesday. Market sources said the much anticipated initial public offering has likely become one of Hong Kong's most popular, with the issue expected to be 900 to 1,000 times subscribed.
The market will be closed on Friday for the Good Friday holiday.
